title: Search and Rescue First Aid Guidance
disclaimer: First aid guidance for bystanders and rescue operators. This guidance is for immediate support only, never a medical diagnosis. All medical decisions require qualified professional care.
note: guidance is the full step for a bystander or the operator, as the source says it. casualty_line is what the robot says to a trapped, conscious casualty (plain words, at most 20, self-care only); a step without one is never said to the casualty. Every source was opened and checked on 2026-11-08 (ref FIRSTAID-SOURCES).

steps.title: Check Breathing
steps.guidance: Check for normal breathing: gently tilt the head back and look, listen, and feel for chest movement and breath for up to 10 seconds.

steps.title: Control Severe Bleeding
steps.guidance: Apply firm, direct pressure on the bleeding wound with a clean cloth or dressing. If an object is embedded, press around it without removing it.
steps.casualty_line: If you can, press a cloth firmly on where it is bleeding, and keep pressing.

steps.title: Do Not Move Neck or Spine
steps.guidance: Do not move the casualty, and do not tell them to move, unless they are in immediate danger. Steady and support the head so the head, neck and spine stay in a straight line until help takes over.
steps.casualty_line: Keep your head and neck still. Do not try to move. Help is coming to you.

steps.title: Place in Recovery Position
steps.guidance: If the casualty is unresponsive but breathing normally and not in danger of spinal trauma, roll them onto their side to keep the airway open.

steps.title: Keep Warm and Prevent Shock
steps.guidance: Cover the casualty with a blanket, jacket, or dry cloth to preserve body warmth and prevent shock. Do not apply direct artificial heat.
steps.casualty_line: Pull anything dry over you to keep warm. We will try to bring you a blanket.

steps.title: Reassure and Monitor
steps.guidance: Stay with the casualty, speak calmly to reassure them, and monitor breathing continuously until emergency medical personnel arrive.

steps.title: Protect Mouth and Nose from Dust
steps.guidance: If trapped, protect the mouth, nose and eyes from airborne debris: cover the mouth and nose with a cloth, clothing or a dust mask. Do not put wet cloth over the nose or mouth.
steps.casualty_line: Cover your mouth and nose with dry cloth and breathe slowly.

steps.title: Keep an Injured Limb Still
steps.guidance: Support the injured limb so it does not move, and keep supporting it until medical help arrives.
steps.casualty_line: Keep the hurt part still. Do not try to move it. Help is coming to you.
